goal: Create the durable, crash-safe, compressed per-participant event-log foundation needed to inspect every job and eventually retry failed work.
recommended_approach: Keep the isolated job-log module, bounded writer queue, partial-file recovery, locking, atomic gzip finalization, retention, and non-fatal error reporting, but define lossless file identities and enforce schema-version compatibility before daemon and CLI consumers depend on version 1.
comparison: The change implements the right architecture cleanly and its 21 focused tests passed. An independent mutation of live-writer detection made `startup_leaves_a_running_log_alone` fail, and restoring the head implementation made it pass; the worktree was then verified clean at the reviewed SHA. It is not yet the best approach because the durable schema cannot reliably distinguish every filename supported by Blit and its reader records—but does not enforce—the schema version.
material_changes: Represent file paths losslessly in all file events, using a structured display-plus-raw representation or a mandatory collision-free encoding with constructors and collision tests.
Make typed reading validate the initial format/version and dispatch through supported-version parsing or migrations, while retaining a separate raw JSON path for retrieval.

findings.title: File events do not preserve Blit's supported raw filename identity
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/job_log.rs:214 — copied, deleted, and failed events contain only a `String` path; crates/blit-core/src/raw_name.rs:5 — Blit's manifest text is explicitly lossy and exact non-UTF-8 bytes are carried separately because distinct names can collapse to the same text.
findings.predicted_failure: Two supported Unix filenames whose invalid UTF-8 bytes collapse to the same replacement text can produce indistinguishable forensic events unless every future caller invents and consistently applies an undocumented escaping convention, violating the requirement to name every affected file.
findings.better_approach: Introduce a `LoggedPath` containing a human-readable value plus optional exact raw bytes encoded for JSON, or formally require one reversible encoding for all paths; provide constructors from native paths and transfer headers and test colliding non-UTF-8 names.

findings.title: The reader ignores the schema version it claims protects compatibility
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/job_log.rs:989 — `open_log` only detects compression, and line 1028 deserializes each line directly as the current `Event`; it never validates the required first `run-start`, `format`, or `version` described at lines 6–11.
findings.predicted_failure: After an incompatible schema bump, an older text reader can silently interpret known event kinds with obsolete semantics or report arbitrary lines as corruption instead of identifying an unsupported version or applying a migration.
findings.better_approach: Read and validate the header before yielding typed events, select a version-specific decoder or migration path, and expose raw-line streaming separately for `--json` retrieval and damaged-log forensics.
